decisions.reason: Retaining the power-board I2C series resistors does not change the interboard connector architecture, connector types, pinout, or physical pin-order policy.
The source concerns series resistors on the I2C lines, not the boost converter enable circuit or switched 5V behavior.
The resistor-retention decision does not alter the board dimensions, orientation, mounting holes, connector placement, or enclosure-fit constraints.
The source does not change the battery connector's placement, orientation, family, pin count, pin functions, or mounting style.
Retaining I2C series resistors has no entailed effect on battery overcharge, overdischarge, thermal, or other protection requirements.
The decision concerns I2C-line protection and does not change battery temperature sensing through the J_BAT NTC connection.
The I2C resistor decision does not affect the GPIO13 SK6812 charge-status indication or the exclusion of a separate charge LED.
Retaining specific I2C series resistors does not change the selected eight-layer board stack.

The source confirms that the existing resistors remain installed but does not change the deferred production-package task, its required capacitor part numbers, or its component-role clarification list.
The source concerns separate I2C series resistors and does not modify the requirement for TVS-based ESD protection.
The resistor-retention decision does not affect the USB-C connector's data-line capability, replacement requirement, or sourceability constraint.
